hook.line: At a neighbourhood meeting nobody wants a vague answer: are you for it or against it? Spanish gives you two short phrases for taking a side.
hook.es: Estoy en contra de que cierren la biblioteca.
hook.en: I'm against them closing the library.

examples.es: Estoy a favor del nuevo parque.
examples.en: I'm in favour of the new park.
Are you for or against? (to a friend)

examples.es: Estoy en contra de que cierren la biblioteca.
examples.en: I'm against them closing the library.

examples.en: Mariana is in favour of talking to Altamira.

examples.es: Don Hernando está en contra de vender el café.
examples.en: Don Hernando is against selling the café.

examples.es: No estoy a favor de que cierren el café.
examples.en: I'm not in favour of them closing the café.

rule:
To take a side, use *estar* plus *a favor de* (for) or *en contra de* (against). After *de* you can put:

a noun: *a favor del parque* (*de* + *el* becomes *del*)
an infinitive: *en contra de vender*
*que* plus a clause: *en contra de que cierren*

That last verb takes the wish form (*cierren*, *abran*), because you are judging something that may or may not happen.

English says "I'm for it" with *be*, and so does Spanish: *estoy*, never *soy*. Keep the *de* before *que*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a prepositional phrase of position. With *que*, the verb that follows is in the subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *a favor* or *en contra* and type the whole sentence. You love the idea: *Estoy ___ del nuevo parque.*
yourTurn.answer: Estoy a favor del nuevo parque.
yourTurn.why: Loving the idea means you are for it: *a favor*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *cierran* or *cierren* and type the whole sentence: *Estoy en contra de que ___ la biblioteca.*
yourTurn.answer: Estoy en contra de que cierren la biblioteca.
yourTurn.why: After *de que* the verb takes the wish form: *cierren*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm in favour of the new park.
yourTurn.answer: Estoy a favor del nuevo parque.
accept: Estoy a favor del parque nuevo.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, asking a friend: Are you for or against?
yourTurn.why: To a friend, *estás*: a side is a state you are in, so *estar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Don Hernando is against selling the café.
yourTurn.answer: Don Hernando está en contra de vender el café.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Estoy a favor de que cierren el café.* Say: I'm not in favour of them closing the café.
yourTurn.answer: No estoy a favor de que cierren el café.
yourTurn.why: Put *no* before *estoy*; the wish form *cierren* stays.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Mariana is in favour of talking to Altamira.
yourTurn.answer: Mariana está a favor de hablar con Altamira.
yourTurn.why: Mariana is one person, so *está*, then *a favor de* and the infinitive.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Taking a side is a position you are in, so Spanish uses *estar*.

pitfalls.wrong: Estoy en contra que cierren la biblioteca.
pitfalls.right: Estoy en contra de que cierren la biblioteca.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *En contra* always needs its *de*, even in front of *que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Estoy en contra de que cierran la biblioteca.
pitfalls.right: Estoy en contra de que cierren la biblioteca.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *de que* the verb switches to the wish form, *cierren*.

personal: Think of one thing in your town you are for or against. Say it with *Estoy a favor de* or *Estoy en contra de*.
